title: Complete Boulevard Alternatives Comparison Sept 2026
summary: This September 2026 guide compares Boulevard alternatives built for medical practices with AI scribe, inventory tracking, and memberships.
body_markdown:
## What Is Boulevard and How Does It Work?


Boulevard started as scheduling and point-of-sale software for salons and beauty businesses. Appointment booking, client management, payment processing through proprietary payment rails, and a self-booking flow for high-volume service businesses form the core of what it does. It is now one of the more widely adopted tools in the[medical spa software](https://decodahealth.com/blog/medical-spa-software) market.


Getting there required expanding well beyond its original salon customer base, and the architecture still reflects where it came from. Chair utilization, retail checkout, and front-desk speed drove the original design decisions.[Boulevard has a 4.6 rating on Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/180087/Boulevard/) across nearly 400 reviews, with users frequently citing its clean booking interface and client communications as strengths.


The clinical layer is where the salon origins start to matter for medical practices. Providers running injectables, weight loss programs, or multi-tier memberships often find the feature set too shallow once they get into daily use. There is no[ambient AI scribe for med spas](https://decodahealth.com/blog/ai-scribe-med-spa-time-savings) , clinical charting built for elective care is absent, and membership configuration does not connect cleanly to checkout. A day spa can work around all of that. A medical practice cannot, because those are the workflows that define the job.


## Why Consider Boulevard Alternatives?


Boulevard fits high-volume aesthetics operations where booking speed and front-desk flow are the top priorities and clinical complexity stays low. Straightforward service menus without fractional dosing or deep membership tiers are where the product does exactly what it promises.


Medical practices run into friction much sooner. A few specific gaps come up repeatedly:


- [Med spa injectable inventory](https://decodahealth.com/blog/med-spa-injectable-inventory-tracking) does not deduct automatically during charting, so counting stock back requires a separate manual step after every treatment.
- Fractional dosing (full, half, quarter syringe) gets handled as separate line items with no true unit-level tracking.
- Membership configuration does not connect cleanly to checkout, confirmed by practices that switched away for exactly this reason.
- There is no native clinical documentation, no AI scribe, and no ambient charting.
- Reporting lacks any meaningful ROI tracking built into the layer.


Payment processing is worth examining on its own. Boulevard owns its payment rails, so confirm your effective per-transaction rate in writing before signing — a point our[high-risk med spa payment processing](https://decodahealth.com/blog/high-risk-processor-med-spa-peptides-semaglutide) guide covers in depth. On a heavy injectable day, those rates accumulate in ways that no pricing page makes obvious upfront.


Practices running semaglutide programs or tiered memberships with real clinical documentation needs feel those gaps every single day. The architecture was built for a different kind of business, and configuration changes can only go so far.


## Best Boulevard Alternatives in September 2026


### 1. Decoda Health


Decoda Health was built from the ground up for independent elective-care practices. Scheduling, clinical documentation, payments, memberships, inventory, and patient communications all run in one system, with AI woven into each module rather than bolted on as a separate tool.


- Ambient AI Scribe generates compliant clinical notes in real time, with custom SOAP templates included
- [Med spa membership programs](https://decodahealth.com/blog/med-spa-membership-pricing-retention) supporting per-item rollover, tiered discounts, and 6-, 10-, and 12-week billing cycles aligned to GLP-1 programs
- AI-powered inventory with photo upload to auto-populate stock and automatic treatment deductions at the point of charting
- High-risk payment processing supporting peptides, ketamine, semaglutide, and TRT/HRT


Best for: Independent elective-care practices with 1 to 20 locations that run membership programs, medical-grade treatments, and clinical documentation in-house.


### 2. Zenoti


Broad multi-location spa and medspa software with scheduling, marketing tools, and reporting. Capable at enterprise scale, but its AI scribe is a separately priced add-on (see our[Decoda Health vs. Zenoti](https://decodahealth.com/compare/zenoti) comparison for details), data exports carry a fee, and support turnaround is measured in weeks, not hours.


Best for: Large chains with dedicated operations staff.


### 3. AestheticsPro


A long-running medspa tool with EMR, scheduling, and consent forms. Recurring complaints include online booking failures that require staff correction calls and unreliable post-appointment texting.


Best for: Practices already on it with low switching appetite.


### 4. Aesthetic Record


Medspa-focused EMR with clinical charting and before-and-after photo management. Membership configuration is a confirmed switching trigger for practices with more complex program structures.


Best for: Practices where clinical photo documentation is the primary workflow priority.


### 5. Mangomint


Salon and spa scheduling software that[moved to a single flat pricing tier](https://www.salontoday.com/articles/mangomint-rolls-out-a-simplified-pricing-model) of $120 per location per month plus $10 per user per month, effective August 2026. No clinical documentation, no EMR, and no high-risk payment processing.


Best for: Non-medical wellness and beauty businesses without clinical requirements.

## Frequently Asked Questions


Why do medical practices look for Boulevard alternatives?


Boulevard was built for salons and day spas, so its architecture reflects those priorities: booking speed, retail checkout, and front-desk flow. Medical practices running injectables, weight loss programs, or tiered memberships hit structural gaps fast: no native clinical documentation, no automatic inventory deduction at charting, and membership configuration that doesn't connect cleanly to checkout.


What features matter most when comparing Boulevard alternatives for a medical practice?


An ambient AI scribe, automatic inventory deduction tied to charting, and membership configuration that supports rollover credits and multi-frequency billing cycles are the capabilities that separate clinical tools from scheduling tools. High-risk payment processing for semaglutide, peptides, and ketamine is also worth confirming before committing, since many platforms simply don't support those transaction types.


When should you consider moving away from Boulevard to a solution like Decoda Health?


The clearest signal is workflow friction at the clinical layer. If your staff is manually counting inventory after every treatment, handling fractional dosing as separate line items, or working around the absence of clinical notes, the architecture isn't built for your practice type. Decoda Health is purpose-built for independent elective-care clinics running exactly those workflows, with AI embedded across scheduling, charting, payments, and memberships in one system.


Is Decoda Health a viable option for practices currently using Boulevard with multi-location operations?


Decoda Health supports 1 to 20 locations under unified reporting, standardized inventory, and consistent membership configuration. The white-glove migration process runs 3 to 4 weeks from contract signing, with the Decoda Health team handling data, appointments, and staff training so the switch doesn't become its own logistical undertaking.


How does Decoda Health's membership configuration differ from what Boulevard offers?


Decoda Health supports per-item rollover, tiered discounts, multi-frequency services, and billing cycles of 6, 10, and 12 weeks. The last three cycle lengths are built for GLP-1 and structured wellness programs. Boulevard has not confirmed native membership-to-checkout linking, which is a recurring reason practices with complex membership programs switch away from it.


How does an AI-native med spa EMR differ from a traditional scheduling tool that adds AI on top?


An AI-native platform like Decoda Health builds intelligence into every workflow from the start — the AI Scribe, AI Front Desk, and inventory deduction all share the same patient record and act on real clinical context. A traditional scheduling tool that adds AI later wraps intelligence around a rigid architecture, so the AI can only act within the limits the original system allows, which typically means a chatbot or a single-module feature, not a connected clinical stack.


Can a single practice management platform replace separate tools for intake forms, scheduling, payments, and patient texting?


Yes — Decoda Health consolidates all four into one system, along with clinical documentation, inventory, memberships, and marketing. Practices that replace five or six disconnected tools report a meaningful reduction in manual data reconciliation, because the patient record is shared across every module rather than siloed in separate logins.


What is the difference between a package and a membership in med spa practice management software, and when should you use each one?


A package is a prepaid bundle of a fixed number of services — a patient buys six laser sessions and redeems them over time. A membership is a recurring subscription that grants ongoing access to services or credits, often with rollover rules, tiered discounts, and a defined billing cycle. Packages work well for single-service commitments; memberships work better when you want predictable monthly revenue and a reason for patients to return on a set schedule.


How do role-based permissions work in a med spa EMR, and can you restrict what front desk staff can see versus what providers can access?


Role-based permissions in Decoda Health let administrators set distinct access levels for receptionists, providers, and administrators — controlling visibility into revenue dashboards, patient chart ratings, clinical dose records, and the ability to override booking limits. Granular controls extend to individual actions like creating, editing, or deleting clinical dose entries, which matters for multi-provider practices managing compliance across staff roles.


How does multi-provider scheduling work across multiple locations — can you see all providers in one calendar view?


Decoda Health supports a unified calendar view across providers and locations, with resource routing built in to account for room and equipment availability alongside provider schedules. Practices can also generate per-provider self-scheduling links, so patients with strong provider loyalty can book directly without navigating the full scheduling flow.


What does post-visit patient communication look like in a med spa platform, and does it require a separate tool?


Decoda Health automates pre- and post-appointment care instructions based on service type, sends them via SMS without a third-party tool, and supports scheduled messaging for follow-up nudges at a future date. Providers can also generate a treatment plan directly from a completed clinical note and deliver it to the patient by email or patient portal in a single step.


What should a practice owner ask during a software demo before committing to a boulevard software alternative for their medical spa?


Ask to see membership configuration taken all the way through to checkout, confirm whether the AI Scribe is included in the base price or sold as an add-on, and verify whether high-risk payment processing for semaglutide and peptides is natively supported. Also confirm how inventory deduction works at the point of charting — if the answer involves a separate manual step, the architecture was not built for medical workflows.


Does replacing boulevard med spa software require buying new phone hardware, or can your existing phone number carry over?


Existing business phone numbers can be ported into Decoda Health, so patient-facing contact information stays consistent through the switch. The AI Front Desk operates as a softphone on-screen rather than requiring physical desk hardware, though physical desk phones can also be configured through the telephony setup process.


How do commission structures work in practice management software — can different providers get different rates by service type or seniority?


Decoda Health supports configurable commission plans that can vary by provider, service type, and service category, with tip prompts also configurable per provider so percentages calculate against that provider's attributed line items. This matters for practices where injectors, aestheticians, and wellness providers all operate under different compensation models within the same clinic.


Is Decoda Health worth evaluating as a boulevard alternative for a plastic surgery or surgical aesthetic practice, or is it built only for med spas?


Decoda Health is built for elective-care practices broadly — including cosmetic surgery and hybrid practices running both aesthetic and medical workflows. The AI Scribe, custom SOAP templates, treatment plan generation from clinical notes, and before-and-after photo comparison tools are all relevant to surgical workflows, though practices with heavy insurance billing should note that Decoda Health is designed for cash-pay and elective care, not insurance-dependent revenue cycles.
